per_probe_support.note: val n = 7; return n. Immutable local binding, no annotation required.
Top-level `var counter: Long = 0` (mutable) and `const val LIMIT: Long = 100` (compile-time constant) in one file.
`val v: Int` declared without initializer; Kotlin definite-assignment analysis accepts assignment in both branches of an if/else before use.

JVM ByteArray/UByteArray constructors always zero-fill; Kotlin has no documented way to obtain genuinely uninitialized bulk storage. R9-named substitution: default-initialized 16-element UByteArray written and measured instead.
`x += 1` compound assignment, in-place scalar mutation.
`xs[1] = 42` on MutableList<Int>, in-place element mutation via operator function set().

Kotlin has no pointer, reference-local, or inout mechanism letting two names in the same scope denote and write the same scalar local storage. No documented feature satisfies any numbered sub-requirement without a container wrapper, which the family's own probes elsewhere (F04.P3) treat separately; no fragment written.
`val window: List<Int> = xs` is a documented non-copying read-only view: Kotlin's read-only collection interfaces are views over the same backing storage, not copies.
Route `first` through a one-element MutableList and read it back as `second`; `val same = (first === second)` uses referential-equality operator `===`, distinct from `equals()`.
Ordinary call `f(x)`; plainest Kotlin call-site syntax, no sigils.

Kotlin has no inout/ref/pointer parameter form letting a callee write a caller's scalar local variable. Canonical task explicitly disallows the mutable-container-wrapper substitute as FULL; per its own text, if no documented way exists no fragment is written.
`val neg: (Int) -> Int = { a -> k - a }` (captures enclosing `k`); `val ys = xs.map(neg)` passes `neg` by name to the standard `map` operation.
`fun mid(xs: List<Int>): Int = xs[1]`; call site binds `val y = mid(xs)`; return y.
`data class DivMod(val q: Int, val r: Int)` (or Pair) with destructuring `val (q, r) = divmod2(a, b)`.
`val r = a * b + c` — ordinary precedence, no parens.
`val q = a / b` (truncating toward zero), `val m = a % b`, `val d = a.toDouble() / b` (Kotlin requires the explicit `.toDouble()`, no implicit widening).

No checked/wrapping/saturating stdlib op exists for Kotlin Int arithmetic; rung (iv) plain operator used: `val o = m + 1` where m=Int.MAX_VALUE. Wrap-around on overflow is JVM/Kotlin-documented behavior (Kotlin spec: 'arithmetic operators do not check for overflow').
Rung (ii): explicit guard `if (b == 0) 0 else a / b`; plain `/` documented to throw ArithmeticException on zero divisor, so guard yields determinate fallback.
`val eq = s1 == s2`; Kotlin `==` on String invokes structural `equals()` (contents), not reference identity.
`xs.sortDescending()` — documented named reverse-ordering in-place extension for MutableList<Int>; `val lt = a < b` scalar comparison.
Rung (ii): `val small = big.toInt()`; ordinary explicit narrowing conversion, documented to keep the low-order 32 bits (silent truncation).
`val sum = i + d`; Kotlin defines an `Int.plus(Double): Double` operator overload so no separate explicit conversion call is required or permitted.
`val e = xs[i]`; documented to throw IndexOutOfBoundsException on out-of-range index (deterministic trap-like exception).
`val part = xs.subList(1, 4)` (documented view, shares backing storage) satisfies the sub-range requirement.
`val o: Int? = null`; `val n = o ?: 0` (Elvis operator, standard optional fallback).
`val h = { a: Int -> a + 1 }`; `val p = o?.let(h)` — safe-call + let is the standard optional-aware chaining form, no explicit if/when.
`fun parseTwice(s: String): Int = s.toInt() * 2`; `String.toInt()` throws NumberFormatException (unchecked, Kotlin has no checked exceptions), propagates automatically.
`val n = try { s.toInt() } catch (e: NumberFormatException) { 0 }`.

`sealed class Shape; data class Circle(val r: Double): Shape(); data class Rect(val w: Double, val h: Double): Shape()`. Kotlin sealed classes restrict all direct subclasses to the same module/package, closing the set to outside units.

`val area: Double = when (s) { is Circle -> 3.141592653589793 * s.r * s.r; is Rect -> s.w * s.h }`; `when` over a sealed hierarchy used as an expression is compiler-enforced exhaustive, no else arm needed.

Open `interface Shape { fun area(): Double }` with `Circle`/`Rect` in unit `shapes`; `Tri` implementing `Shape` from a separate compilation unit; dispatch through the `Shape`-typed value. Kotlin interfaces are open by default and implementable from any unit.
`fun <T> head(xs: List<T>): T = xs[0]`; called at List<Int> and List<String>; declared result type is T, not erased to Any.
`fun <T : Comparable<T>> maxOf2(a: T, b: T): T = if (a > b) a else b` — declaration-site bound `T : Comparable<T>`.
`interface Named { fun tag(): String }`; `class A`, `class B` implement it; `val items: List<Named> = listOf(A(), B())`; `items[0].tag()` dispatches at runtime via interface vtable.
`val xs = mutableListOf(1, 2, 3)`; `val total = xs.sum()` (standard stdlib reduction).
`val mp = mutableMapOf("a" to 1)`; `val total = mp.values.sum()`; `val miss = mp.getOrDefault("b", 0)`.
`File("data.txt").bufferedReader().use { r -> ... }` — `Closeable.use` guarantees close() exactly once on every exit path including exceptions, standard-library scoped cleanup.

Kotlin/JVM has no deterministic destructor/deinit hook (finalize() is deprecated/nondeterministic). Nearest standard construct per the probe's own named substitution: implement Closeable and invoke close() deterministically via a scoped `use {}` block.
`println("x")` — kotlin.io is implicitly available without an explicit import.

File `util.kt`: top-level `fun pubAdd(a: Int, b: Int): Int = a + b + secret()` and `private fun secret(): Int = 1` (Kotlin top-level `private` is file-scoped, enforcing the boundary even within the same module). Multi-unit recipe used per toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes.
`kotlin.concurrent.thread { ... }` (stdlib wrapper over java.lang.Thread) launches two units; `.join()` on both; combine results. Part of kotlin-stdlib bundled with `-include-runtime`.

`java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong` (JDK class always available to a Kotlin/JVM program) with `incrementAndGet()`; documented atomic read-modify-write, race-free by specification. Verified pattern: 2 threads x 1000 increments = 2000.

Kotlin/JVM under the frozen recipe (kotlinc ... -include-runtime; java -jar) has no built-in FFI to call a C function without JNI native compilation (separate toolchain/build step) or the preview java.lang.foreign API (requires --enable-preview beyond the frozen recipe). No fragment written.

Kotlin/JVM's frozen recipe produces a JAR of JVM bytecode, not a native compiled artifact with linker symbols; there is no documented mechanism to export a stable unmangled C-ABI symbol named `add2`. nm field: 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe' (N-1 per na_policy/support_rubric NONE criteria).
